newsitem.title: USA: Rhone-Poulenc profits rise; stock off on recall fears.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc profits rise; stock off on recall fears.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc., the U.S. unit of France's Rhone-Poulenc SA, Wednesday reported higher profits for the latest quarter but its stock fell on concern over the impact of a plasma product recall.
Rhone-Poulenc was off $2.50 at $70.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
The company reported third quarter earnings of $97.4 million, or 72 cents a share, vs. year ago earnings of $81.5 million, or 61 cents a share.
But it said that a voluntary recall of Albuminar and Plasma Plex by Centeon LLC, a joint venture with Hoechst AG had cut its earnings for the latest quarter by 17 cents a share.
"There's some nervousness about whether or not the recalled products will make it back to market in a timely manner," said Robert Uhl, an analyst at Salomon Brothers.
The company also said that its fourth quarter results would be impacted by lost sales of the products, which it said it did not expect to resume shipping before January.
There are investor worries that the products' return to the market would be delayed beyond the fourth quarter.
The recall announced early this month stemmed from concern about the risk of bacterial contamination due to vials cracked in transit.
